headline_marked: 9-wicket crush: [[Bangladesh beat world's top-ranked Australia]] in Darwin
headline: 9-wicket crush: Bangladesh beat world's top-ranked Australia in Darwin
summary: Australia coach Andrew McDonald admits standards 'slipped' after a shock home Test loss to the Tigers
details: Bangladesh secured a massive victory in Darwin, crushing the world's top-ranked Australian side by nine wickets in the first home Test of the series.
Australia coach Andrew McDonald admitted that the team "let our standards slip" after failing to score 500 runs over two innings on the surface.
The defeat has sparked calls for a top-order overhaul in the Australian squad, with former captain Ricky Ponting leading the demand for change.
Opener Jake Weatherald and number three Marnus Labuschagne are under significant pressure following repeated failures in the match.
Coach McDonald defended his ageing squad, stating that the players still have "a fair bit of cricket left in them" despite the loss.
The Australian team is now facing tough decisions regarding squad changes as they prepare for the second Test in Mackay on Saturday.
Potential replacements for the top order include Matt Renshaw and several young players like Sam Konstas and Cooper Connolly.
caption:
A shock 9-wicket win! Bangladesh crushes the world's top-ranked Australia in Darwin.

Bangladesh secured a massive victory in Darwin, crushing the world's top-ranked Australian side by nine wickets in the first home Test of the series.

Australia coach Andrew McDonald admitted that the team "let our standards slip" after failing to score 500 runs over two innings on the surface.

The defeat has sparked calls for a top-order overhaul in the Australian squad, with former captain Ricky Ponting leading the demand for change.

Opener Jake Weatherald and number three Marnus Labuschagne are under significant pressure following repeated failures in the match.

Coach McDonald defended his ageing squad, stating that the players still have "a fair bit of cricket left in them" despite the loss.

The Australian team is now facing tough decisions regarding squad changes as they prepare for the second Test in Mackay on Saturday.

Potential replacements for the top order include Matt Renshaw and several young players like Sam Konstas and Cooper Connolly.

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Measles: [[Death toll hits 915]] as 7 more die in 24 hours
headline: Measles: Death toll hits 915 as 7 more die in 24 hours
summary: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 1,031 new cases with measles symptoms were reported in a single day.
details: Seven people died within 24 hours (Sunday 8 AM to Monday 8 AM) after exhibiting symptoms of measles, according to a regular report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Monday.
During the same period, 1,031 new people showed symptoms of measles, while 50 cases were laboratory-confirmed.
Since March 15, a total of 915 people have died, including 816 children who died with measles symptoms and 99 children who died from confirmed measles.
The total number of people showing symptoms of measles since March 15 has reached 143,778, with 17,930 cases being laboratory-confirmed.
A total of 125,386 people were admitted to hospitals with measles symptoms since March 15, of which 120,913 have recovered and been discharged.
caption:
915 deaths and over 143,000 symptomatic cases since March. Measles is surging in Bangladesh.

Seven people died within 24 hours (Sunday 8 AM to Monday 8 AM) after exhibiting symptoms of measles, according to a regular report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Monday.

During the same period, 1,031 new people showed symptoms of measles, while 50 cases were laboratory-confirmed.

Since March 15, a total of 915 people have died, including 816 children who died with measles symptoms and 99 children who died from confirmed measles.

The total number of people showing symptoms of measles since March 15 has reached 143,778, with 17,930 cases being laboratory-confirmed.

A total of 125,386 people were admitted to hospitals with measles symptoms since March 15, of which 120,913 have recovered and been discharged.
